identity.title: UGC 4211: A Confirmed Dual Active Galactic Nucleus in the Local Universe at 230 pc Nuclear Separation

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using Hubble Space Telescope/STIS, VLT/MUSE+AO, Keck/OSIRIS+AO spectroscopy, and ALMA observations, we show that the spatial distribution, optical and NIR emission lines, and millimeter continuum emission are all consistent with both nuclei being powered by accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs).

UGC 4211 was observed by ALMA on 2021 October 24 and 2022 August 19 in band 6 (\approx230 GHz; program ID 2021.1.01019.S, PI: Treister), aimed to study the molecular gas contents of nearby major galaxy mergers in the BAT AGN sample.

evidence.quote: We present multiwavelength high-spatial resolution (\sim0.1'', 70 pc) observations of UGC 4211 at z=0.03474, a late-stage major galaxy merger at the closest nuclear separation yet found in near-IR imaging (0''32, \sim230 pc projected separation).
It was previously classified as a Sy 2 system at z=0.03474 or \sim153 Mpc (cite: Koss:2022:2) based on stellar absorption lines

question.value: Whether the two close-separation (~230 pc) near-IR nuclei in the late-stage major galaxy merger UGC 4211 are both powered by accreting supermassive black holes (a confirmed dual AGN).

evidence.quote: Using Hubble Space Telescope/STIS, VLT/MUSE+AO, Keck/OSIRIS+AO spectroscopy, and ALMA observations, we show that the spatial distribution, optical and NIR emission lines, and millimeter continuum emission are all consistent with both nuclei being powered by accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs).
We focus in this Letter on the dual AGN nature of the two NIR nuclei.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure ALMA 231 GHz nuclear continuum positions, flux densities, separation, and spectral index

method.value: Coadd line-free channels in four spectral windows (221-240 GHz) to make high-resolution (~0''.07 and ~0''.04 with robust -0.5) continuum maps, and fit spatial 2D Gaussian models using CASA imfit.

evidence.quote: The continuum map analyzed here was computed coadding emission in line-free regions in four ALMA spectral windows ranging from 221 to 240 GHz
Using the CASA imfit task to fit model Gaussians spatially, we find two sources of continuum emission consistent with the northern and southern nuclei (both in separation and position angle).
The nuclear ALMA 231 GHz continuum emission (<200 pc), has been found to be a good proxy of the AGN luminosity
Both sources are unresolved at this resolution, and remain unresolved on a higher resolution, \sim0''04 (28 pc), map obtained using a Briggs robust parameter of -0.5.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract and fit optical and NIR nuclear emission line spectra and BPT diagnostics

method.value: Extract 1D spectra from HST/STIS (0''.25 x 0''.2), Keck/OSIRIS (0''.3 diameter apertures), and VLT/MUSE (three 0''.15 diameter apertures N, S, M and Voronoi-binned spaxels), fit continuum and Gaussian emission lines, and place line ratios on BPT diagrams.

evidence.quote: We extracted a 5 pixel (0''25) spectrum along the N–S direction across the nuclei peak \[O iii\] emission in HST/STIS which is at similar separation to the two NIR nuclei (0''3).
With the excellent pixel sampling and PSF of VLT/MUSE, we extract three smaller spectral apertures (0''15 diameter) with two centered on the NIR nuclei and an additional region midway between them

We use PySpecKit to fit the optical emission lines from HST/STIS, the MUSE \[O iii\] \lambda 5007 map, and the NIR emission lines from Keck/OSIRIS, which uses a Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm for spectral fitting (cite: Ginsburg:2011:1109.001) with Gaussians following the approach of (cite: Koss:2017:74).

analysis_steps.goal: Test for dual X-ray point sources, X-ray variability, and 22 GHz radio continuum counterpart

method.value: Fit Chandra image with ChaRT PSF + 2D Gaussian and run BAYMAX to compute Bayes factor for two vs. one point source; analyze Chandra and NuSTAR light curves with XRONOS lcstats; self-calibrate and fit JVLA 22 GHz continuum with CASA imfit.

evidence.quote: We then used BAYMAX (cite: 2019ApJ...877...17F) to search for the presence of two X-ray point sources.
To search for the hard X-ray variability within observations in Chandra and NuSTAR, we use lcstats task from the XRONOS (version 6.0) package to analyze the light curves.
Using CASA task imfit the centroid position of the single detection is R.A.=08:04:46.391, decl.=+10:46:36.01 with a flux of 3.74\pm0.017 mJy within 6^{\prime \prime} and 3.2741\pm0.0072 mJy.

key_parameters.value: Chandra subpixel repositioning 0''.25 pix^-1; BAYMAX 20''x20'' box and 1''x1'' prior box; light curve 500s bins; JVLA gaincal solint 180 s

evidence.quote: We analyze the 0.5-8 keV counts within a 20^{\prime \prime}x 20^{\prime \prime}(40 x 40 sky pixel) box centered on UGC 4211.
We impose a solution interval of 180 s, and apply the these temporal gains to the data set using applycal.

assumptions.value: Uniform spatial priors on primary and secondary X-ray source positions in BAYMAX (full 20''x20'' FOV or 1''x1'' boxes around IR cores)

evidence.quote: We first allow \mu_{\mathrm{primary}} and \mu_{\mathrm{secondary}} to be anywhere within this field of view (represented by x, y, priors that are uniform distributions across the full extent of the sky x, y range).

We then rerun our analysis constraining the \mu_{\mathrm{primary}} and \mu_{\mathrm{secondary}} via x,y priors that are uniform and constrained to a 1 x 1^{\prime \prime}(2 x 2 sky pixel) box centered on the observed locations of each resolved IR stellar core.

fitting.value: 2D Gaussian + PSF fitting for Chandra; Bayesian likelihood (Bayes factor) in BAYMAX; 2D Gaussian fitting with CASA imfit for JVLA

evidence.quote: When fitting the Chandra data with the PSF and a 2D Gaussian, we find evidence of a extended emission
BAYMAX calculates the likelihood (Bayes factor, calculated in natural log space, hereafter \log{\mathcal{BF_{2/1}}}) that Chandra observations are composed of two versus one point source.

validation.value: Comparison with BAYMAX simulation suite sensitivity limits for separations 0''.30 < r < 0''.35

findings_qualitative.value: Both the northern and southern nuclei of UGC 4211 are unresolved (<28 pc) in ALMA 231 GHz continuum, spatially coincident with the two NIR stellar nuclei separated by ~230 pc.

evidence.quote: Both sources are unresolved at this resolution, and remain unresolved on a higher resolution, \sim0''04 (28 pc), map obtained using a Briggs robust parameter of -0.5.
Therefore, the position, separation, and PA of the NIR nuclei closely match the 2 millimeter (mm) sources given the relative astrometric and centroiding errors (\sim0''1).

findings_qualitative.value: The southern nucleus exhibits a hidden broad-line region in NIR hydrogen recombination lines (Pa beta, Br gamma) and a flat mm spectral index (alpha = 0.02 +/- 0.26), while the northern nucleus shows peak [O III] emission and harder Seyfert BPT ionization ratios.

evidence.quote: A hidden broad-line region (BLR) component (>1000 km s^{-1}) is also found in the NIR hydrogen recombination lines (e.g. Pa\beta, FWHM=1996\pm180 km s^{-1}; Br\gamma, FWHM=2530\pm160 km s^{-1}) of the southern nucleus, but no BLR is found in the northern nucleus.

The high-resolution MUSE AO (and HST/STIS) observations, show two separate emission sources of \[O iii\] \lambda 5007, each of them unresolved at \sim0''1 resolution. When placed on the BPT diagram, both nuclei are clearly in the Seyfert locus with the northern AGN further in the ionized AGN region.

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA CO(2-1) and MUSE CaT stellar absorption velocity maps show matching velocity gradients and a ~150 km s^-1 velocity offset between the two nuclei, proving they are kinematically independent nuclei rather than jet knots.

evidence.quote: Using the CO(2-1) emission line as a tracer of the molecular gas, the velocity map shows a clear velocity gradient centered on the positions of the northern and southern continuum emitters. A similar gradient is also seen in the Ca II \,\lambda 8498, 8542, 8662 stellar absorption lines. This demonstrates that both sources are kinematically independent nuclei, while rules out other possibilities, such as a jet knots.

claims.hypothesis: Both close-separation (~230 pc) NIR nuclei in the late-stage merger UGC 4211 host active, accreting supermassive black holes (a dual AGN).
claims.experiment: Multiwavelength high-spatial resolution (~0''.04–0''.1) observations combining ALMA 231 GHz continuum and CO(2-1) kinematics, VLT/MUSE+AO, HST/STIS, and Keck/OSIRIS+AO spectroscopy.
claims.result: Detection of two compact (<28 pc) ALMA 231 GHz continuum point sources matching the two NIR nuclei (separation 0''.33 +/- 0''.01 or 229 +/- 7 pc), NIR broad recombination lines in the southern nucleus, Seyfert BPT line ratios in both nuclei with stronger [O III] peaking on the northern nucleus, and independent velocity gradients in CO(2-1) and Ca II stellar absorption with a ~150 km s^-1 offset.
claims.finding: UGC 4211 is confirmed as a dual AGN at 230 pc projected separation with similar black hole masses (log M_BH/M_sun ~ 8.1 and ~ 8.3-8.4).

evidence.quote: Using Hubble Space Telescope/STIS, VLT/MUSE+AO, Keck/OSIRIS+AO spectroscopy, and ALMA observations, we show that the spatial distribution, optical and NIR emission lines, and millimeter continuum emission are all consistent with both nuclei being powered by accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs).
We find that our multiwavelength observations confirm the presence of two active nuclei in the center of UGC 4211, separated by 230 pc (projected) and \sim150 km s^{-1} (along our line-of-sight)

claims.hypothesis: The millimeter continuum and optical emission of the northern nucleus could arise from compact star formation, shocks, or photoionization by the single broad-line AGN in the southern nucleus.
claims.experiment: Measure spatial compactness of ALMA 231 GHz continuum at ~0''.04 (28 pc) resolution, compare mm luminosity to X-ray AGN scaling relations, and examine [O III] peak location and BPT ratios.
claims.result: Both ALMA continuum sources are unresolved at <28 pc with luminosities matching X-ray selected AGN and far exceeding expectations for star formation in that volume; [O III] peaks directly on the northern nucleus with harder Seyfert ionization than the heavily obscured southern nucleus.
claims.finding: Star formation, shocks, and single-AGN cross-ionization scenarios are ruled out or highly unlikely.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the mm continuum luminosity is consistent with the expected value for bright nearby X-ray selected AGN emission following the (cite: 2022ApJ...938...87K) correlation, and is significantly higher than the values expected for star formation processes in such a small size.

The single AGN scenario, where the narrow emission-line region associated with the northern NIR nucleus is photoionized by the broad-line AGN in the southern nucleus, seems highly unlikely, given the \[O iii\] emission peaks on the center of the northern nucleus where the ALMA continuum source also confirms the AGN nature.

claims.hypothesis: The SMBH pair in UGC 4211 will form a gravitationally bound binary and merge within a Hubble time rather than stalling.
claims.experiment: Estimate binary hardening rates from dynamical friction, stellar hardening, gas-driven inspiral, and GW emission following Goulding et al. (2019) from 230 pc separation.
claims.result: The binary will harden in <= 1 Myr, reach the GW-dominated regime in ~1 Gyr via stellar hardening alone, or reach milliparsec scales (PTA band) in ~200 Myr if gas-driven inspiral is efficient.
claims.finding: UGC 4211 will reach the GW-dominated phase well within a Hubble time, significantly faster than stalled binaries.

evidence.quote: We estimate UGC 4211 will harden in \lesssim 1~\rm{Myr}.

We estimate that, in the absence of efficient gas-driven inspiral, it will take UGC 4211 \sim 1~\rm{Gyr} to reach GW dominated evolution, but significantly shorter than the merger timescale for ‘stalled’ binaries (cite: Kelley:2018:964). If enough gas is present it can reduce this time, reaching milliparsec scales in \sim 200~\rm{Myr}

why_this_data.value: Subkpc dual AGN in late-stage mergers are heavily obscured and separated by ~0''.3, requiring high-spatial resolution (~0''.06-0''.1) multiwavelength data (NIR AO, optical AO IFS, and ALMA mm continuum/CO) to resolve both nuclei and avoid false positives from single diagnostics.

evidence.quote: Ultimately, it is critical to identify subkpc dual AGN using a multiwavelength analysis to confirm the nature of their nuclei.
The nuclear ALMA 231 GHz continuum emission (<200 pc), has been found to be a good proxy of the AGN luminosity, with a tight correlation with the 14–150 keV (cite: 2022ApJ...938...87K).

why_this_method.value: Extracting 0''.15 MUSE apertures and applying Voronoi spatial binning (S/N=35 for stellar kinematics, S/N=10 for [O III]) ensures sufficient S/N for weak Hbeta fitting and unbiased velocity dispersion measurements.

evidence.quote: This is done because the individual spaxels are too low S/N to perform emission line fitting of the weak H\beta emission.

Unbiased measurements of stellar kinematics require a minimum S/N, so for an adaptive spatial-binning scheme we use the Voronoi algorithm as implemented in vorbin (cite: 2003MNRAS.342..345C), requiring a S/N of 35 for each bin.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Star formation as the origin of the compact nuclear mm continuum emission (rejected due to <30 pc size, flat spectral index, and Seyfert BPT ratios).

evidence.quote: While this could be due to star formation, the fact that they are spatially extremely compact,  <30 pc, and (at least the south nucleus) consistent with a flat, nonthermal, spectrum, strongly suggests that these signals arise from mm wave emission, as seen in X-ray selected AGN (cite: 2022ApJ...938...87K).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Jet knots as the origin of the two nuclei (ruled out by independent velocity gradients in CO(2-1) and Ca II stellar absorption lines centered on the nuclei).

evidence.quote: This demonstrates that both sources are kinematically independent nuclei, while rules out other possibilities, such as a jet knots.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single AGN in the southern nucleus photoionizing the northern narrow-line region or shock ionization (rejected because [O III] and ALMA continuum peak on the northern nucleus, the southern nucleus is heavily obscured in optical-UV, and shocks only move H II regions into composite/LINER loci).

evidence.quote: The single AGN scenario, where the narrow emission-line region associated with the northern NIR nucleus is photoionized by the broad-line AGN in the southern nucleus, seems highly unlikely, given the \[O iii\] emission peaks on the center of the northern nucleus where the ALMA continuum source also confirms the AGN nature.
